opportunity: kuna's built-in prototype tables share one width-stable type vocabulary, so all 108 aggregate-pointer slots in them are spelled `void *`. `void *` never matches a ground-truth `FILE *` (the metric's width-only generosity has no pointer entry), and named-struct pointers are 22.5% of matchable GT variables -- a class kuna scores 0.0% on while ida scores 432 / ghidra 382 / binja 523 TP on the same 92-binary sample. The libc/POSIX-namable slice of it is ~4.1% of matchable GT (FILE 605 occurrences, stat 255, passwd 136).
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-libctypes.xml (9 assertions over three `load file` passes on two real ELFs; #5/#6 pin that the DWARF layout of `stat` survives the option being on) + 15 table-invariant unit tests in analyzers::protos::kuna_libctypes::tests (including the incomplete-shell adopt rule and the width-stable fall-back of a declined name) + kuna-cli/tests/decompile_project_cli.rs (header_syntax_checks_when_a_type_shares_a_name_with_a_function) + kuna-console project::tests::typedef_names_reads_every_declarator_shape
inspiration: Ghidra ApplyDataArchiveAnalyzer applying generic_clib_64.gdt, whose FILE */struct stat * slots carry the header's own pointee; signatures reduced from `gcc -aux-info` over the platform headers (_GNU_SOURCE + _FORTIFY_SOURCE=2); widths from sizeof/_Alignof

table.held_name_rule: the pass runs AFTER DwarfPass, so a name already held is the platform's own. It is adopted when it is a struct of the DECLARED WIDTH -- under the name, or under the spelling the platform's headers use for it (FILE -> _IO_FILE). Anything else declines the signature: a different width is a program's own type sharing the spelling, a zero-width forward declaration would restore the PTRSUB hazard, and completing or re-keying another owner's shell would strand every pointer already minted against it (set_fields_struct clones into a new Rc).
table.width_abi: glibc x86-64 (sizeof/_Alignof). On another ABI a width can be a few bytes off, which can only change whether an access renders as a field or as a cast; the name is ABI-independent and a wrong width cannot make a pointer point at the wrong thing.
table.pass_order_rule: registered after DwarfPass and seeded from IMPORTED names only (LibProtoPass also matches a name the image DEFINES), so a DWARF-defined function's prototype is never outranked by a table entry.

selection_rule: a retarget restates a shipped signature with the same arity and variadic slot, so it needs no new evidence; a NEW name needs a machine-readable declaration (`gcc -aux-info`) AND corpus weight, measured as PLT call sites over the 524 stripped O0+O2 decbench ELFs. Kept: rewind 117, __uflow 77, fgetc 57, freopen 32, funlockfile 20, getdelim 18, flockfile 18, popen 17, pclose 17. Rejected: fgetc_unlocked 0, fmemopen 0, __underflow 0 (and no installed declaration to reduce).

benchmark.note: re-measured after the DWARF-order fix: identical (+39 perfect, 0 moved off perfect, 386 improved of which 39 reached perfect, 0 worsened). The scored surface is stripped binaries, and `decompile-all` output there is byte-identical before and after that fix on all 7 sweep binaries, in both arms.
benchmark.spelling_and_the_metric: The scored surface is the STRIPPED image (typesweep decompiles `stripped_of(unstripped)` and takes ground truth from the twin), and there no DWARF type is held, so the table mints and prints the bare `FILE` -- `normalize_type('FILE *') & normalize_type('FILE *')` = {'FILE *','FILE*'}, a match. On a `-g` image the adopted definition is the platform's own and prints under ITS tag, `_IO_FILE *`; that spelling is NOT accepted for a ground-truth `FILE *` -- decbench/metrics/type_match.py `_POINTEE_MAP` (built from TYPE_MAP) has no `_IO_FILE` row, so `normalize_type('_IO_FILE *') & normalize_type('FILE *')` is empty. No measurement in this record runs on an unstripped image, so nothing here is affected; a future one over `-g` images would score every adopted stream slot a miss, and the fix for that is the metric's alias table, not a second spelling of the type.

corpus_sweep.method: `kuna decompile-all` off vs opaque over 7 stripped binaries (fmt/ls/grep/gzip/tar O2, find/diff O0), every changed line put in a bucket plus a control-flow/call/constant skeleton comparison per function; full output and the residual-bucket shape histogram in corpus-hunk-classification.txt
corpus_sweep.classification: every inspected skeleton difference is an offset constant becoming a field name or an `&` replacing a cast; two representative cases are improvements (diffutils 0x10e15 collapses 20 scattered stack slots into one on-stack struct sigaction; gzip 0x65d0 types the localtime result `tm *`). No hunk changes a call target, a control-flow edge or a numeric literal.

piece_accessor_form.what: `vN._off_size_`, an aggregate slot read as a sub-piece. It appears wherever a value is typed as an aggregate that has no field at the offset being touched: always for the fieldless shells this option mints, and also for the program's own on-stack aggregates once a `stat *`/`sigaction *` argument pulls their scattered slots into one object. Off, the same reads are casts or separate slots.
piece_accessor_form.reading: +229 (+22.9%) over the 7 sweep binaries, concentrated in tar/grep/gzip/find/diff; ls goes DOWN by one. Same class as the `field_0x` count in the -g sweep -- an offset that was a cast becoming a slot of a named pointee. The follow-up `glibc` value, which gives the stream shell real field names, retires the stdio half of it.

export_c_cost.what: `kuna decompile-project` writes a `.c` alongside the `.h`. The exported body has never compiled (it is a reading aid, not a rebuildable source tree), but this option makes it measurably less so: the named shells stay `type_incomplete`, so the `.h` declares `typedef struct FILE FILE; /* opaque */` while the `.c` declares objects of that type and reads fields out of them. The PR's export claim covers the `.h` only.
export_c_cost.method: kuna decompile-project <O2/coreutils/stripped/ls> -o D --option libctypes off|opaque ; cc -std=c99 -fsyntax-only -I D D/ls.c 2>&1 | grep -c 'error:'
export_c_cost.new_error_classes: 7 classes absent from the off arm, 57 errors; the remaining +1 is three pre-existing classes moving by one each. (A plain uniq -c over the raw message text reports more classes for the same 58 errors, because gcc's `did you mean` hint and each pointee spelling vary inside one class.)

from_the_type_name_function_name_clash_i.sites: ls.c:177 (sigaction), ls.c:558 (stat), ls.c:2375 `sigaction(v6,NULL,(sigaction *)v3);`, ls.c:2405. The header fix in this PR resolves the clash in `build_header` only; `build_body` still emits the colliding definition.

export_c_cost.header_unaffected: `cc -std=c99 -fsyntax-only` on the exported .h: 0 errors in BOTH arms on the stripped ls. The header fix itself was re-verified on the UNSTRIPPED ls with the DEFAULT arm, this branch's binary against the main tree's: 15 header errors -> 8, the 7 removed being `stat`/`statx` `redeclared as different kind of symbol` and the 5 `expected declaration specifiers ... before 'stat'` that follow it. The 8 that remain are one pre-existing class in both trees (a `.`-bearing DWARF name in a declarator). That claim stands; it is the .c that is not covered by it.
export_c_cost.retired_by: the follow-up `glibc` value (public `_IO_FILE`/`stat` field layouts instead of an opaque shell) retires the three incomplete-typedef classes; the name-clash-in-the-body half is a `build_body` question this PR does not answer.

intrinsic_form.what: `SUBxy(`/`CONCATxy(` -- the functional forms the printer falls back to for a sub-piece or a concatenation it cannot spell as C. Counted because `PTRSUB(` alone does not cover the class.
intrinsic_form.reading: net +3 across 3,702 functions (find +2 SUB, tar -1 SUB / +2 CONCAT): the same slot read through a different decomposition, never a new one. `PTRSUB(` stays 0/0 everywhere, which is the form the sizing rule exists to prevent.

by_value_named_aggregates.what: `Ty::NamedPtr` is pointer-only, but that is a property of the TABLE, not of the emitted C: propagation still carries a named type into a by-value position. The sized shell, not the pointer, is what keeps that out of the hidden-return-buffer classification.
by_value_named_aggregates.method: grep each arm's whole-binary output over the same 7 sweep binaries for a named aggregate in a declarator position, and for `rethidden`
by_value_named_aggregates.by_value_returns_on_detail: ls 0x10210, gzip 0x10bb0, tar 0x43230 -- all the same gnulib `gettime` wrapper, all `timespec`, all correct: a 16-byte timespec is returned in RAX:RDX. off renders the same function `undefined16 sub_10210(void) { char v1 [16]; ... return v1._0_16_; }`.
by_value_named_aggregates.widest_named_type_in_a_return_slot: 16 (timespec). No stat (144), sigaction (152) or FILE (216) reaches one anywhere in the corpus -- a corpus observation, not an invariant the table enforces.
